correctness.rationale: Because a permutation has one occurrence of each symbol per period, a query uniquely fixes its residue phases. Every admissible gap residue has a unique least representative in the first min(q,b_i-a_i+1) legal differences. The independent minima form the componentwise earliest embedding, and tuples (first phase, minimal gap differences) biject with distinct locally feasible queries. Their endpoint generating polynomial is exactly Q; coefficient truncation at qk-1 yields the finite-host count. The unique maximal endpoint gives the saturation boundary; inclusion-exclusion verifies the uniform binomial form. Self-contained independent query enumeration passed 1472 uniform and 4000 variable-bound instances. Finite tests corroborate rather than constitute the infinite proof.

value.rationale: For the natural interval-gap subsequence model, the theorem gives a complete all-parameter distinct-language census for repeated permutation hosts, with an explicit product generating polynomial and sharp finite-host saturation and universality boundaries. This addresses exactly the multiplicity-of-embeddings obstacle of language enumeration and identifies a q-sized residue transition, rather than computing one ad hoc small example or a routine fixed-query membership test.
